1: # Syntax in rust-analyzer
2: 
3: ## About the guide
4: 
5: This guide describes the current state of syntax trees and parsing in
6: rust-analyzer as of 2020-01-09, pinned to commit
7: [syntax-2020-01-09]. It is a reference document: it does not walk through the
8: code step by step, but instead describes the architecture and the models used,
9: so that reading the actual source code becomes easier.
10: 
11: [syntax-2020-01-09]: https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/tree/cf5bdf464cad7ceb9a67e07985a3f4d3799ec0b6
12: 
13: ## Source Code
14: 
15: The implementation lives in three places:
16: 
17: * [rowan] is a generic library for syntax trees. It doesn't know anything about
18:   Rust: it only deals with `SyntaxKind`s, nodes and tokens, and implements the
19:   tree data structure (storage, traversal, incremental re-parsing).
20: 
21: * [ra_syntax] is a crate which glues `rowan` to Rust. It defines the Rust
22:   specific `SyntaxKind` enum, the `ast` module (a typed API on top of the raw
23:   tree), the lexer for Rust tokens and the `SyntaxTreeBuilder` which the parser
24:   drives.
25: 
26: * [ra_parser] is a crate for the actual parsing. It is deliberately kept
27:   separate from the rest of the codebase, so that the parser does not even know
28:   about the concrete tree implementation.
29: 
30: [rowan]: https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan
31: [ra_syntax]: ../../crates/ra_syntax/src/lib.rs
32: [ra_parser]: ../../crates/ra_parser/src/lib.rs
33: 
34: ## Design Goals
35: 
36: The design of the syntax tree and the parser is driven by the following goals:
37: 
38: * **Lossless trees are a must.** This is in direct contrast with many other
39:   compilers, which may freely drop whitespace, comments and even grammar nodes.
40:   rust-analyzer does not: converting any text into a syntax tree and back is a
41:   total identity function. All comments and all whitespace are explicitly
42:   represented in the tree. This is important for IDE features like refactoring
43:   and syntax highlighting, and it's the reason why the tree stores the full
44:   text.
45: 
46: * **Syntax trees are semantic-less.** They describe the *shape* of the file, not
47:   its meaning. The tree has no notion of name resolution, types or even a
48:   distinction between "a function" and "a list". All such analysis lives higher
49:   in the stack (in `ra_hir`), and operates on different, position-independent
50:   representations derived from the tree.
51: 
52: * **Syntax trees are simple value types.** A tree is immutable, has no notion of
53:   identity, and is cheap to create and to share. Keeping a reference to a single
54:   node keeps the whole enclosing file alive.
55: 
56: * **Syntax trees have an intuitive traversal API.** You can move from any node
57:   to any other node using `parent`, `(next|prev)_sibling`, `children`,
58:   `ancestors` and `descendants`. Nodes know their text range in the file.
59: 
60: * **Parsing is resilient.** Even wildly invalid input still produces a syntax
61:   tree which captures all the available information. All accessor methods return
62:   `Option`s, to account for incomplete code. The tree for `fn foo` contains a
63:   function definition with `None` for the parameter list and `None` for the
64:   body.
65: 
66: * **Parsing is performant.** The tree is recreated on every keystroke and the
67:   parser should handle typical files in a few milliseconds. To achieve this, we
68:   use `unsafe` in a number of hot paths and support incremental re-parsing of
69:   the affected subtree (see `Parse::reparse`). Performance is a hard requirement
70:   which justifies the use of `unsafe` code.
71: 
72: * **Parsing is isolated.** The parser does not know about the tree
73:   representation. It works over abstract `TokenSource` and `TreeSink` traits
74:   (see [ra_parser]), which makes the parsing logic reusable and easy to reason
75:   about in isolation.
76: 
77: ## Trees
78: 
79: ### Overview
80: 
81: The syntax tree is represented in three layers, stacked on top of each other:
82: 
83: * **GreenNodes** -- the data-carrying layer. The green tree is the durable,
84:   immutable "source of truth". Only green nodes and green tokens store actual
85:   data: kinds and full token text. Removing a green subtree from the tree is
86:   the only operation that can be done on the green layer.
87: 
88: * **SyntaxNodes** -- the view layer. Syntax nodes are cheap on-demand
89:   "red" views over the green tree, which add parent pointers and an absolute
90:   text range. They are created (in O(depth)) just by looking at a green node
91:   and are cheap to throw away and recreate.
92: 
93: * **AST** -- the semantic layer. Typed wrappers around syntax nodes which
94:   provide a high-level API, like `fn_def.name()` or `block.expr()`, on top of
95:   the raw untyped tree.
96: 
97: This is a so-called [red-green] structure: the durable, immutable data lives in
98: "green" nodes, while the ephemeral views which are recomputed on demand are
99: "red". Only the green layer stores data; the two other layers only store
100: pointers and compute things lazily.
101: 
102: [red-green]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-dev-guide/blob/c5d21bd76d475bb32ff8d3cdf77bb4dc7e0df901/src/incremental-compilation.html
103: 
104: ### GreenNode
105: 
106: Conceptually, the green tree is a functional, untyped, immutable tree of nodes
107: and tokens. Nodes have a kind and a list of children (which are nodes or
108: tokens), tokens have a kind and text:
109: 
110: ```rust
111: /// The `SyntaxKind` enum is the vocabulary of the tree: a list of all kinds
112: /// a node or a token can have.
113: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
114: pub enum SyntaxKind {
115:     // ... tokens, produced by the lexer:
116:     WHITESPACE,
117:     IDENT,
118:     INT_NUMBER,
119:     PLUS,
120:     // ...
121:     // ... nodes, produced by the parser:
122:     SOURCE_FILE,
123:     FN_DEF,
124:     NAME,
125:     PARAM_LIST,
126:     BLOCK_EXPR,
127:     BLOCK,
128:     BIN_EXPR,
129:     // ...
130: }
131: 
132: /// A node or a token, unified in a single type for traversal.
133: enum SyntaxElement {
134:     Node(Node),
135:     Token(Token),
136: }
137: 
138: /// A node is a dumb container of children.
139: struct Node {
140:     kind: SyntaxKind,
141:     children: Vec<SyntaxElement>,
142: }
143: 
144: /// A token is a leaf, and carries the whole text.
145: struct Token {
146:     kind: SyntaxKind,
147:     text: SmolStr,
148: }
149: ```
150: 
151: In reality, the tree is more cleverly implemented for performance: green nodes
152: are stored behind `Arc`, and the actual concrete types are `rowan::GreenNode`
153: and `rowan::GreenToken` (re-exported from `crates/ra_syntax/src/syntax_node.rs`).
154: But the structure above is exactly the model.
155: 
156: A few notes about the design:
157: 
158: * The tree is *untyped*. There is nothing in the data structure which would
159:   enforce that a `NAME` node contains an `IDENT` token. The parser and a set of
160:   standalone `validation` functions (see `crates/ra_syntax/src/validation`) are
161:   the only things which guarantee the shape of the tree. This is done
162:   deliberately: it keeps the tree a simple value type, and pushes all checks
163:   out of the data structure.
164: 
165: * *Tokens carry full text.* Node text is not stored: the text of a node is
166:   defined as the concatenation of the texts of all tokens in the node's
167:   subtree. `SyntaxText` computes this lazily, which makes getting the text of a
168:   node cheap and preserves the invariant that tree-to-text is an identity
169:   function.
170: 
171: * *Errors are data.* `SourceFile::parse` always returns a syntax tree, even for
172:   completely invalid files. Errors which the parser recovers from are encoded
173:   into the tree itself as `ERROR` nodes (the `ERROR` variant of `SyntaxKind`),
174:   and reported separately as a list of `SyntaxError`s attached to the `Parse`
175:   result. `Parse::ok` succeeds only if there are no errors.
176: 
177: As a concrete example, consider the input
178: 
179: ```
180: fn f() { 90 + 2 }
181: ```
182: 
183: The resulting tree looks like this (this is the `Debug` output of the tree as
184: produced by `Parse::debug_dump`; `KIND@[start; end)` is a node with its text
185: range, and tokens additionally show their text):
186: 
187: ```
188: SOURCE_FILE@[0; 17)
189:   FN_DEF@[0; 17)
190:     FN_KW@[0; 2) "fn"
191:     WHITESPACE@[2; 3) " "
192:     NAME@[3; 4)
193:       IDENT@[3; 4) "f"
194:     PARAM_LIST@[4; 6)
195:       L_PAREN@[4; 5) "("
196:       R_PAREN@[5; 6) ")"
197:     WHITESPACE@[6; 7) " "
198:     BLOCK_EXPR@[7; 17)
199:       BLOCK@[7; 17)
200:         L_CURLY@[7; 8) "{"
201:         WHITESPACE@[8; 9) " "
202:         BIN_EXPR@[9; 15)
203:           LITERAL@[9; 11)
204:             INT_NUMBER@[9; 11) "90"
205:           WHITESPACE@[11; 12) " "
206:           PLUS@[12; 13) "+"
207:           WHITESPACE@[13; 14) " "
208:           LITERAL@[14; 15)
209:             INT_NUMBER@[14; 15) "2"
210:         WHITESPACE@[15; 16) " "
211:         R_CURLY@[16; 17) "}"
212: ```
213: 
214: Note how every single character of the input appears in the tree exactly once:
215: this is the "lossless" property. Note also how `90 + 2` is a `BIN_EXPR`
216: ("binary expression") node with `LITERAL` children wrapping `INT_NUMBER`
217: tokens, and note that the final expression of a block is not wrapped into an
218: `EXPR_STMT` node -- the tree faithfully reflects the fact that `90 + 2` is the
219: *value* of the block (as opposed to a statement with a semicolon).
220: 
221: ### SyntaxNode
222: 
223: The `SyntaxNode` and `SyntaxToken` types (type aliases for
224: `rowan::SyntaxNode<RustLanguage>` / `rowan::SyntaxToken<RustLanguage>`, see
225: `crates/ra_syntax/src/syntax_node.rs`) are red, view-layer nodes.
226: 
227: Each syntax node holds a reference to the green data of its subtree plus useful
228: computed properties: a pointer to the parent red node, an absolute text range
229: and a `SyntaxKind`. Traversing a red node gives you other red nodes, so the
230: whole red tree is created lazily, on demand:
231: 
232: ```rust
233: // The whole file is alive as long as you keep one node:
234: let file = parse.tree().syntax();              // red root, over the whole file
235: let node = file.descendants().next().unwrap(); // some child, absolutely positioned
236: 
237: // Moving around:
238: let parent = node.parent();
239: let next = node.next_sibling_or_token();
240: let children: Vec<_> = node.children().collect();
241: 
242: // Ranges and text:
243: let range: TextRange = node.text_range();
244: let text: SyntaxText = node.text();
245: ```
246: 
247: Both `SyntaxNode` and `SyntaxToken` are cheap `Arc`-based handles, and can be
248: unified into the `SyntaxElement` type, which powers the "with tokens" traversal
249: methods (`children_with_tokens`, `preorder_with_tokens`, ...). The `algo`
250: module in `ra_syntax` provides generic tree algorithms on top of these, most
251: notably `walk` -- an O(1) stack space traversal.
252: 
253: Nodes do not store the identity of the file they came from; they only know
254: about the text.
255: 
256: ### AST
257: 
258: The AST layer (`crates/ra_syntax/src/ast`) is a typed facade over the raw tree.
259: Types like `ast::FnDef`, `ast::Name`, `ast::BinExpr` wrap a `SyntaxNode`, and
260: provide structured accessors:
261: 
262: ```rust
263: let func = ast::FnDef::cast(node)?;   // `AstNode::cast` checks the kind
264: let name = func.name()?.text();       // typed getters return `Option`s
265: ```
266: 
267: The two key traits are `AstNode` (`cast` from a `SyntaxNode`) and `AstToken`
268: (`cast` from a `SyntaxToken`). The AST types are generated from the
269: [grammar.ron] description of the grammar by `cargo xtask codegen` (see
270: `crates/ra_syntax/src/ast/generated.rs`). Because the parser is resilient, all
271: AST accessors return `Option`s, and enums like `ast::Expr` are used to group
272: related nodes together and to match on them (see the `match_ast!` macro in
273: `crates/ra_syntax/src/lib.rs`).
274: 
275: [grammar.ron]: ../../crates/ra_syntax/src/grammar.ron

40: fn get_inlay_hints(
41:     acc: &mut Vec<InlayHint>,
42:     sb: &mut SourceBinder<RootDatabase>,
43:     file_id: FileId,
44:     node: &SyntaxNode,
45:     max_inlay_hint_length: Option<usize>,
46: ) -> Option<()> {
47:     let _p = profile("get_inlay_hints");
48:     let db = sb.db;
49:     let analyzer = Lazy::new(move || sb.analyze(hir::InFile::new(file_id.into(), node), None));
50:     match_ast! {
51:         match node {
52:             ast::LetStmt(it) => {
53:                 if it.ascribed_type().is_some() {
54:                     return None;
55:                 }
56:                 let pat = it.pat()?;
57:                 get_pat_type_hints(acc, db, &analyzer, pat, false, max_inlay_hint_length);
58:             },
59:             ast::LambdaExpr(it) => {
60:                 it.param_list().map(|param_list| {
61:                     param_list
62:                         .params()
63:                         .filter(|closure_param| closure_param.ascribed_type().is_none())
64:                         .filter_map(|closure_param| closure_param.pat())
65:                         .for_each(|root_pat| get_pat_type_hints(acc, db, &analyzer, root_pat, false, max_inlay_hint_length))
66:                 });
67:             },

69:                 let pat = it.pat()?;
70:                 get_pat_type_hints(acc, db, &analyzer, pat, false, max_inlay_hint_length);
71:             },
72:             ast::IfExpr(it) => {
73:                 let pat = it.condition()?.pat()?;
74:                 get_pat_type_hints(acc, db, &analyzer, pat, true, max_inlay_hint_length);
75:             },
76:             ast::WhileExpr(it) => {
77:                 let pat = it.condition()?.pat()?;

79:             },

81:                 it.arms()
82:                     .map(|match_arm| match_arm.pats())
83:                     .flatten()
84:                     .for_each(|root_pat| get_pat_type_hints(acc, db, &analyzer, root_pat, true, max_inlay_hint_length));

98: fn get_param_name_hints(
99:     acc: &mut Vec<InlayHint>,
100:     db: &RootDatabase,
101:     analyzer: &SourceAnalyzer,
102:     expr: ast::Expr,
103: ) -> Option<()> {
104:     let args = match &expr {
105:         ast::Expr::CallExpr(expr) => expr.arg_list()?.args(),
106:         ast::Expr::MethodCallExpr(expr) => expr.arg_list()?.args(),
107:         _ => return None,
108:     };
109: 
110:     let mut parameters = get_fn_signature(db, analyzer, &expr)?.parameter_names.into_iter();
111: 
112:     if let ast::Expr::MethodCallExpr(_) = &expr {
113:         parameters.next();
114:     };
115: 
116:     let hints = parameters
117:         .zip(args)
118:         .filter_map(|(param, arg)| {
119:             if arg.syntax().kind() == SyntaxKind::LITERAL && !param.is_empty() {
120:                 Some((arg.syntax().text_range(), param))
121:             } else {
122:                 None
123:             }
124:         })
125:         .map(|(range, param_name)| InlayHint {
126:             range,
127:             kind: InlayKind::ParameterHint,
128:             label: param_name.into(),
129:         });
130: 
131:     acc.extend(hints);
132:     Some(())
133: }

135: fn get_fn_signature(
136:     db: &RootDatabase,
137:     analyzer: &SourceAnalyzer,
138:     expr: &ast::Expr,
139: ) -> Option<FunctionSignature> {
140:     match expr {
141:         ast::Expr::CallExpr(expr) => {
142:             // FIXME: Type::as_callable is broken for closures
143:             let callable_def = analyzer.type_of(db, &expr.expr()?)?.as_callable()?;
144:             match callable_def {
145:                 hir::CallableDef::FunctionId(it) => {
146:                     let fn_def = it.into();
147:                     Some(FunctionSignature::from_hir(db, fn_def))
148:                 }
149:                 hir::CallableDef::StructId(it) => FunctionSignature::from_struct(db, it.into()),
150:                 hir::CallableDef::EnumVariantId(it) => {
151:                     FunctionSignature::from_enum_variant(db, it.into())
152:                 }
153:             }
154:         }
155:         ast::Expr::MethodCallExpr(expr) => {
156:             let fn_def = analyzer.resolve_method_call(&expr)?;
157:             Some(FunctionSignature::from_hir(db, fn_def))
158:         }
159:         _ => None,
160:     }
161: }

163: fn get_pat_type_hints(
164:     acc: &mut Vec<InlayHint>,
165:     db: &RootDatabase,
166:     analyzer: &SourceAnalyzer,
167:     root_pat: ast::Pat,
168:     skip_root_pat_hint: bool,
169:     max_inlay_hint_length: Option<usize>,
170: ) {
171:     let original_pat = &root_pat.clone();
172: 
173:     let hints = get_leaf_pats(root_pat)
174:         .into_iter()
175:         .filter(|pat| !skip_root_pat_hint || pat != original_pat)
176:         .filter_map(|pat| {
177:             let ty = analyzer.type_of_pat(db, &pat)?;
178:             if ty.is_unknown() {
179:                 return None;
180:             }
181:             Some((pat.syntax().text_range(), ty))
182:         })
183:         .map(|(range, pat_type)| InlayHint {
184:             range,
185:             kind: InlayKind::TypeHint,
186:             label: pat_type.display_truncated(db, max_inlay_hint_length).to_string().into(),
187:         });
188: 
189:     acc.extend(hints);
190: }

192: fn get_leaf_pats(root_pat: ast::Pat) -> Vec<ast::Pat> {
193:     let mut pats_to_process = std::collections::VecDeque::<ast::Pat>::new();
194:     pats_to_process.push_back(root_pat);
195: 
196:     let mut leaf_pats = Vec::new();
197: 
198:     while let Some(maybe_leaf_pat) = pats_to_process.pop_front() {
199:         match &maybe_leaf_pat {
200:             ast::Pat::BindPat(bind_pat) => match bind_pat.pat() {
201:                 Some(pat) => pats_to_process.push_back(pat),
202:                 _ => leaf_pats.push(maybe_leaf_pat),
203:             },
204:             ast::Pat::TuplePat(tuple_pat) => pats_to_process.extend(tuple_pat.args()),
205:             ast::Pat::RecordPat(record_pat) => {
206:                 if let Some(pat_list) = record_pat.record_field_pat_list() {
207:                     pats_to_process.extend(
208:                         pat_list
209:                             .record_field_pats()
210:                             .filter_map(|record_field_pat| {
211:                                 record_field_pat
212:                                     .pat()
213:                                     .filter(|pat| pat.syntax().kind() != SyntaxKind::BIND_PAT)
214:                             })
215:                             .chain(pat_list.bind_pats().map(|bind_pat| {
216:                                 bind_pat.pat().unwrap_or_else(|| ast::Pat::from(bind_pat))
217:                             })),
218:                     );
219:                 }
220:             }
221:             ast::Pat::TupleStructPat(tuple_struct_pat) => {
222:                 pats_to_process.extend(tuple_struct_pat.args())
223:             }
224:             ast::Pat::RefPat(ref_pat) => pats_to_process.extend(ref_pat.pat()),
225:             _ => (),
226:         }
227:     }
228:     leaf_pats
229: }

298: /// WatchThread exists to wrap around the communication needed to be able to
299: /// run `cargo check` without blocking. Currently the Rust standard library
300: /// doesn't provide a way to read sub-process output without blocking, so we
301: /// have to wrap sub-processes output handling in a thread and pass messages
302: /// back over a channel.
303: /// The correct way to dispose of the thread is to drop it, on which the
304: /// sub-process will be killed, and the thread will be joined.
305: struct WatchThread {
306:     handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
307:     message_recv: Receiver<CheckEvent>,
308: }
309: 
310: enum CheckEvent {
311:     Begin,
312:     Msg(cargo_metadata::Message),
313:     End,
314: }
315: 
316: impl WatchThread {
317:     fn dummy() -> WatchThread {
318:         WatchThread { handle: None, message_recv: never() }
319:     }
320: 
321:     fn new(options: &CheckOptions, workspace_root: &PathBuf) -> WatchThread {
322:         let mut args: Vec<String> = vec![
323:             options.command.clone(),
324:             "--message-format=json".to_string(),
325:             "--manifest-path".to_string(),
326:             format!("{}/Cargo.toml", workspace_root.to_string_lossy()),
327:         ];
328:         if options.all_targets {
329:             args.push("--all-targets".to_string());
330:         }
331:         args.extend(options.args.iter().cloned());
332: 
333:         let (message_send, message_recv) = unbounded();
334:         let enabled = options.enable;
335:         let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
336:             if !enabled {
337:                 return;
338:             }
339: 
340:             let mut command = Command::new("cargo")
341:                 .args(&args)
342:                 .stdout(Stdio::piped())
343:                 .stderr(Stdio::null())
344:                 .spawn()
345:                 .expect("couldn't launch cargo");
346: 
347:             // If we trigger an error here, we will do so in the loop instead,
348:             // which will break out of the loop, and continue the shutdown
349:             let _ = message_send.send(CheckEvent::Begin);
350: 
351:             for message in cargo_metadata::parse_messages(command.stdout.take().unwrap()) {
352:                 let message = match message {
353:                     Ok(message) => message,
354:                     Err(err) => {
355:                         log::error!("Invalid json from cargo check, ignoring: {}", err);
356:                         continue;
357:                     }
358:                 };
359: 
360:                 match message_send.send(CheckEvent::Msg(message)) {
361:                     Ok(()) => {}
362:                     Err(_err) => {
363:                         // The send channel was closed, so we want to shutdown
364:                         break;
365:                     }
366:                 }
367:             }
368: 
369:             // We can ignore any error here, as we are already in the progress
370:             // of shutting down.
371:             let _ = message_send.send(CheckEvent::End);
372: 
373:             // It is okay to ignore the result, as it only errors if the process is already dead
374:             let _ = command.kill();
375: 
376:             // Again, we don't care about the exit status so just ignore the result
377:             let _ = command.wait();
378:         });
379:         WatchThread { handle: Some(handle), message_recv }
380:     }
381: }
382: 
383: impl std::ops::Drop for WatchThread {
384:     fn drop(&mut self) {
385:         if let Some(handle) = self.handle.take() {
386:             // Replace our reciever with dummy one, so we can drop and close the
387:             // one actually communicating with the thread
388:             let recv = std::mem::replace(&mut self.message_recv, never());
389: 
390:             // Dropping the original reciever initiates thread sub-process shutdown
391:             drop(recv);
392: 
393:             // Join the thread, it should finish shortly. We don't really care
394:             // whether it panicked, so it is safe to ignore the result
395:             let _ = handle.join();
396:         }
397:     }
398: }

201: /// Converts a Rust root diagnostic to LSP form
202: ///
203: /// This flattens the Rust diagnostic by:
204: ///
205: /// 1. Creating a LSP diagnostic with the root message and primary span.
206: /// 2. Adding any labelled secondary spans to `relatedInformation`
207: /// 3. Categorising child diagnostics as either `SuggestedFix`es,
208: ///    `relatedInformation` or additional message lines.
209: ///
210: /// If the diagnostic has no primary span this will return `None`
211: pub(crate) fn map_rust_diagnostic_to_lsp(
212:     rd: &RustDiagnostic,
213:     workspace_root: &PathBuf,
214: ) -> Option<MappedRustDiagnostic> {
215:     let primary_span = rd.spans.iter().find(|s| s.is_primary)?;
216: 
217:     let location = map_span_to_location(&primary_span, workspace_root);
218: 
219:     let severity = map_level_to_severity(rd.level);
220:     let mut primary_span_label = primary_span.label.as_ref();
221: 
222:     let mut source = String::from("rustc");
223:     let mut code = rd.code.as_ref().map(|c| c.code.clone());
224:     if let Some(code_val) = &code {
225:         // See if this is an RFC #2103 scoped lint (e.g. from Clippy)
226:         let scoped_code: Vec<&str> = code_val.split("::").collect();
227:         if scoped_code.len() == 2 {
228:             source = String::from(scoped_code[0]);
229:             code = Some(String::from(scoped_code[1]));
230:         }
231:     }
232: 
233:     let mut related_information = vec![];
234:     let mut tags = vec![];
235: 
236:     // If error occurs from macro expansion, add related info pointing to
237:     // where the error originated
238:     if !is_from_macro(&primary_span.file_name) && primary_span.expansion.is_some() {
239:         let def_loc = map_span_to_location_naive(&primary_span, workspace_root);
240:         related_information.push(DiagnosticRelatedInformation {
241:             location: def_loc,
242:             message: "Error originated from macro here".to_string(),
243:         });
244:     }
245: 
246:     for secondary_span in rd.spans.iter().filter(|s| !s.is_primary) {
247:         let related = map_secondary_span_to_related(secondary_span, workspace_root);
248:         if let Some(related) = related {
249:             related_information.push(related);
250:         }
251:     }
252: 
253:     let mut suggested_fixes = vec![];
254:     let mut message = rd.message.clone();
255:     for child in &rd.children {
256:         let child = map_rust_child_diagnostic(&child, workspace_root);
257:         match child {
258:             MappedRustChildDiagnostic::Related(related) => related_information.push(related),
259:             MappedRustChildDiagnostic::SuggestedFix(suggested_fix) => {
260:                 suggested_fixes.push(suggested_fix)
261:             }
262:             MappedRustChildDiagnostic::MessageLine(message_line) => {
263:                 write!(&mut message, "\n{}", message_line).unwrap();

265:                 // These secondary messages usually duplicate the content of the
266:                 // primary span label.
267:                 primary_span_label = None;
268:             }
269:         }
270:     }
271: 
272:     if let Some(primary_span_label) = primary_span_label {
273:         write!(&mut message, "\n{}", primary_span_label).unwrap();
274:     }

276:     if is_unused_or_unnecessary(rd) {

280:     if is_deprecated(rd) {

282:     }

285:         range: location.range,
286:         severity,
287:         code: code.map(NumberOrString::String),
288:         source: Some(source),
289:         message,
290:         related_information: if !related_information.is_empty() {
291:             Some(related_information)
292:         } else {
293:             None
294:         },
295:         tags: if !tags.is_empty() { Some(tags) } else { None },
296:     };

298:     Some(MappedRustDiagnostic { location, diagnostic, suggested_fixes })

334:         Ok(url)

336:         Ok(Url::from_file_path(&path)

55: pub fn main_loop(
56:     ws_roots: Vec<PathBuf>,
57:     client_caps: ClientCapabilities,
58:     config: ServerConfig,
59:     connection: Connection,
60: ) -> Result<()> {
61:     log::info!("server_config: {:#?}", config);
62: 
63:     let mut loop_state = LoopState::default();
64:     let mut world_state = {
65:         let feature_flags = {
66:             let mut ff = FeatureFlags::default();
67:             for (flag, value) in config.feature_flags {
68:                 if ff.set(flag.as_str(), value).is_err() {
69:                     log::error!("unknown feature flag: {:?}", flag);
70:                     show_message(
71:                         req::MessageType::Error,
72:                         format!("unknown feature flag: {:?}", flag),
73:                         &connection.sender,
74:                     );
75:                 }
76:             }
77:             ff
78:         };
79:         log::info!("feature_flags: {:#?}", feature_flags);
80: 
81:         // FIXME: support dynamic workspace loading.
82:         let workspaces = {
83:             let mut loaded_workspaces = Vec::new();
84:             for ws_root in &ws_roots {
85:                 let workspace = ra_project_model::ProjectWorkspace::discover_with_sysroot(
86:                     ws_root.as_path(),
87:                     config.with_sysroot,
88:                     &config.cargo_features,
89:                 );
90:                 match workspace {
91:                     Ok(workspace) => loaded_workspaces.push(workspace),
92:                     Err(e) => {
93:                         log::error!("loading workspace failed: {}", e);
94:                         if let Some(ra_project_model::CargoTomlNotFoundError(_)) = e.downcast_ref()
95:                         {
96:                             if !feature_flags.get("notifications.cargo-toml-not-found") {
97:                                 continue;
98:                             }
99:                         }
100:                         show_message(
101:                             req::MessageType::Error,
102:                             format!("rust-analyzer failed to load workspace: {}", e),
103:                             &connection.sender,
104:                         );
105:                     }
106:                 }
107:             }
108:             loaded_workspaces
109:         };
110: 
111:         let globs = config
112:             .exclude_globs
113:             .iter()
114:             .map(|glob| ra_vfs_glob::Glob::new(glob))
115:             .collect::<std::result::Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
116: 
117:         if config.use_client_watching {
118:             let registration_options = req::DidChangeWatchedFilesRegistrationOptions {
119:                 watchers: workspaces
120:                     .iter()
121:                     .flat_map(|ws| ws.to_roots())
122:                     .filter(|root| root.is_member())
123:                     .map(|root| format!("{}/**/*.rs", root.path().display()))
124:                     .map(|glob_pattern| req::FileSystemWatcher { glob_pattern, kind: None })
125:                     .collect(),
126:             };
127:             let registration = req::Registration {
128:                 id: "file-watcher".to_string(),
129:                 method: "workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles".to_string(),
130:                 register_options: Some(serde_json::to_value(registration_options).unwrap()),
131:             };
132:             let params = req::RegistrationParams { registrations: vec![registration] };
133:             let request =
134:                 request_new::<req::RegisterCapability>(loop_state.next_request_id(), params);
135:             connection.sender.send(request.into()).unwrap();
136:         }
137: 
138:         let options = {
139:             let text_document_caps = client_caps.text_document.as_ref();
140:             Options {
141:                 publish_decorations: config.publish_decorations,
142:                 supports_location_link: text_document_caps
143:                     .and_then(|it| it.definition)
144:                     .and_then(|it| it.link_support)
145:                     .unwrap_or(false),
146:                 line_folding_only: text_document_caps
147:                     .and_then(|it| it.folding_range.as_ref())
148:                     .and_then(|it| it.line_folding_only)
149:                     .unwrap_or(false),
150:                 max_inlay_hint_length: config.max_inlay_hint_length,
151:                 cargo_watch: CheckOptions {
152:                     enable: config.cargo_watch_enable,
153:                     args: config.cargo_watch_args,
154:                     command: config.cargo_watch_command,
155:                     all_targets: config.cargo_watch_all_targets,
156:                 },
157:             }
158:         };
159: 
160:         WorldState::new(
161:             ws_roots,
162:             workspaces,
163:             config.lru_capacity,
164:             &globs,
165:             Watch(!config.use_client_watching),
166:             options,
167:             feature_flags,
168:         )
169:     };
170: 
171:     let pool = ThreadPool::new(THREADPOOL_SIZE);
172:     let (task_sender, task_receiver) = unbounded::<Task>();
173:     let (libdata_sender, libdata_receiver) = unbounded::<LibraryData>();
174: 
175:     log::info!("server initialized, serving requests");
176:     {
177:         let task_sender = task_sender;
178:         let libdata_sender = libdata_sender;
179:         loop {
180:             log::trace!("selecting");
181:             let event = select! {
182:                 recv(&connection.receiver) -> msg => match msg {
183:                     Ok(msg) => Event::Msg(msg),
184:                     Err(RecvError) => Err("client exited without shutdown")?,
185:                 },
186:                 recv(task_receiver) -> task => Event::Task(task.unwrap()),
187:                 recv(world_state.task_receiver) -> task => match task {
188:                     Ok(task) => Event::Vfs(task),
189:                     Err(RecvError) => Err("vfs died")?,
190:                 },
191:                 recv(libdata_receiver) -> data => Event::Lib(data.unwrap()),
192:                 recv(world_state.check_watcher.task_recv) -> task => match task {
193:                     Ok(task) => Event::CheckWatcher(task),
194:                     Err(RecvError) => Err("check watcher died")?,
195:                 }
196:             };
197:             if let Event::Msg(Message::Request(req)) = &event {
198:                 if connection.handle_shutdown(&req)? {
199:                     break;
200:                 };
201:             }
202:             loop_turn(
203:                 &pool,
204:                 &task_sender,
205:                 &libdata_sender,
206:                 &connection,
207:                 &mut world_state,
208:                 &mut loop_state,
209:                 event,
210:             )?;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:     log::info!("waiting for tasks to finish...");
215:     task_receiver.into_iter().for_each(|task| {
216:         on_task(task, &connection.sender, &mut loop_state.pending_requests, &mut world_state)
217:     });
218:     libdata_receiver.into_iter().for_each(drop);
219:     log::info!("...tasks have finished");
220:     log::info!("joining threadpool...");
221:     drop(pool);
222:     log::info!("...threadpool has finished");
223: 
224:     let vfs = Arc::try_unwrap(world_state.vfs).expect("all snapshots should be dead");
225:     drop(vfs);
226: 
227:     Ok(())
228: }

244: impl fmt::Debug for Event {
245:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
246:         let debug_verbose_not = |not: &Notification, f: &mut fmt::Formatter| {
247:             f.debug_struct("Notification").field("method", &not.method).finish()
248:         };
249: 
250:         match self {
251:             Event::Msg(Message::Notification(not)) => {
252:                 if notification_is::<req::DidOpenTextDocument>(not)
253:                     || notification_is::<req::DidChangeTextDocument>(not)
254:                 {
255:                     return debug_verbose_not(not, f);
256:                 }
257:             }
258:             Event::Task(Task::Notify(not)) => {
259:                 if notification_is::<req::PublishDecorations>(not)
260:                     || notification_is::<req::PublishDiagnostics>(not)
261:                 {
262:                     return debug_verbose_not(not, f);
263:                 }
264:             }
265:             Event::Task(Task::Respond(resp)) => {
266:                 return f
267:                     .debug_struct("Response")
268:                     .field("id", &resp.id)
269:                     .field("error", &resp.error)
270:                     .finish();
271:             }
272:             _ => (),
273:         }
274:         match self {
275:             Event::Msg(it) => fmt::Debug::fmt(it, f),
276:             Event::Task(it) => fmt::Debug::fmt(it, f),
277:             Event::Vfs(it) => fmt::Debug::fmt(it, f),
278:             Event::Lib(it) => fmt::Debug::fmt(it, f),
279:             Event::CheckWatcher(it) => fmt::Debug::fmt(it, f),
280:         }
281:     }
282: }

307: fn loop_turn(
308:     pool: &ThreadPool,
309:     task_sender: &Sender<Task>,
310:     libdata_sender: &Sender<LibraryData>,
311:     connection: &Connection,
312:     world_state: &mut WorldState,
313:     loop_state: &mut LoopState,
314:     event: Event,

318:     // NOTE: don't count blocking select! call as a loop-turn time
319:     let _p = profile("main_loop_inner/loop-turn");

651: impl<'a> PoolDispatcher<'a> {
652:     /// Dispatches the request onto the current thread
653:     fn on_sync<R>(
654:         &mut self,
655:         f: fn(&mut WorldState, R::Params) -> Result<R::Result>,
656:     ) -> Result<&mut Self>
657:     where
658:         R: req::Request + 'static,
659:         R::Params: DeserializeOwned + panic::UnwindSafe + 'static,
660:         R::Result: Serialize + 'static,
661:     {
662:         let (id, params) = match self.parse::<R>() {
663:             Some(it) => it,

665:                 return Ok(self);
666:             }
667:         };
668:         let world = panic::AssertUnwindSafe(&mut *self.world);
669:         let task = panic::catch_unwind(move || {
670:             let result = f(world.0, params);
671:             result_to_task::<R>(id, result)
672:         })
673:         .map_err(|_| format!("sync task {:?} panicked", R::METHOD))?;
674:         on_task(task, self.msg_sender, self.pending_requests, self.world);

678:     /// Dispatches the request onto thread pool
679:     fn on<R>(&mut self, f: fn(WorldSnapshot, R::Params) -> Result<R::Result>) -> Result<&mut Self>
680:     where
681:         R: req::Request + 'static,
682:         R::Params: DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static,
683:         R::Result: Serialize + 'static,
684:     {
685:         let (id, params) = match self.parse::<R>() {
686:             Some(it) => it,
687:             None => {
688:                 return Ok(self);
689:             }
690:         };
691: 
692:         self.pool.execute({
693:             let world = self.world.snapshot();
694:             let sender = self.sender.clone();
695:             move || {
696:                 let result = f(world, params);
697:                 let task = result_to_task::<R>(id, result);
698:                 sender.send(task).unwrap();
699:             }
700:         });
701: 
702:         Ok(self)
703:     }
704: 
705:     fn parse<R>(&mut self) -> Option<(RequestId, R::Params)>
706:     where
707:         R: req::Request + 'static,
708:         R::Params: DeserializeOwned + 'static,
709:     {
710:         let req = self.req.take()?;
711:         let (id, params) = match req.extract::<R::Params>(R::METHOD) {
712:             Ok(it) => it,

718:         self.pending_requests.start(PendingRequest {

726:     fn finish(&mut self) {

729:             Some(req) => {

734:                     "unknown request".to_string(),

60: /// Return all the assists applicable at the given position.
61: ///
62: /// Assists are returned in the "unresolved" state, that is only labels are
63: /// returned, without actual edits.
64: pub fn applicable_assists<H>(db: &H, range: FileRange) -> Vec<AssistLabel>
65: where
66:     H: HirDatabase + 'static,
67: {
68:     AssistCtx::with_ctx(db, range, false, |ctx| {
69:         assists::all()
70:             .iter()
71:             .filter_map(|f| f(ctx.clone()))
72:             .map(|a| match a {
73:                 Assist::Unresolved { label } => label,
74:                 Assist::Resolved { .. } => unreachable!(),
75:             })
76:             .collect()
77:     })
78: }
79: 
80: /// Return all the assists applicable at the given position.
81: ///
82: /// Assists are returned in the "resolved" state, that is with edit fully
83: /// computed.
84: pub fn assists<H>(db: &H, range: FileRange) -> Vec<ResolvedAssist>
85: where
86:     H: HirDatabase + 'static,
87: {
88:     use std::cmp::Ordering;
89: 
90:     AssistCtx::with_ctx(db, range, true, |ctx| {
91:         let mut a = assists::all()
92:             .iter()
93:             .filter_map(|f| f(ctx.clone()))
94:             .map(|a| match a {
95:                 Assist::Resolved { assist } => assist,
96:                 Assist::Unresolved { .. } => unreachable!(),
97:             })
98:             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
99:         a.sort_by(|a, b| match (a.get_first_action().target, b.get_first_action().target) {
100:             (Some(a), Some(b)) => a.len().cmp(&b.len()),
101:             (Some(_), None) => Ordering::Less,
102:             (None, Some(_)) => Ordering::Greater,
103:             (None, None) => Ordering::Equal,
104:         });
105:         a
106:     })
107: }

18:     Resolved { assist: ResolvedAssist },

21: /// `AssistCtx` allows to apply an assist or check if it could be applied.
22: ///
23: /// Assists use a somewhat over-engineered approach, given the current needs. The
24: /// assists workflow consists of two phases. In the first phase, a user asks for
25: /// the list of available assists. In the second phase, the user picks a
26: /// particular assist and it gets applied.
27: ///
28: /// There are two peculiarities here:
29: ///
30: /// * first, we ideally avoid computing more things then necessary to answer
31: ///   "is assist applicable" in the first phase.
32: /// * second, when we are applying assist, we don't have a guarantee that there
33: ///   weren't any changes between the point when user asked for assists and when
34: ///   they applied a particular assist. So, when applying assist, we need to do
35: ///   all the checks from scratch.
36: ///
37: /// To avoid repeating the same code twice for both "check" and "apply"
38: /// functions, we use an approach reminiscent of that of Django's function based
39: /// views dealing with forms. Each assist receives a runtime parameter,
40: /// `should_compute_edit`. It first check if an edit is applicable (potentially
41: /// computing info required to compute the actual edit). If it is applicable,
42: /// and `should_compute_edit` is `true`, it then computes the actual edit.
43: ///
44: /// So, to implement the original assists workflow, we can first apply each edit
45: /// with `should_compute_edit = false`, and then applying the selected edit
46: /// again, with `should_compute_edit = true` this time.
47: ///
48: /// Note, however, that we don't actually use such two-phase logic at the
49: /// moment, because the LSP API is pretty awkward in this place, and it's much
50: /// easier to just compute the edit eagerly :-)
51: #[derive(Debug)]
52: pub(crate) struct AssistCtx<'a, DB> {
53:     pub(crate) db: &'a DB,
54:     pub(crate) frange: FileRange,
55:     source_file: SourceFile,
56:     should_compute_edit: bool,
57: }
58: 
59: impl<'a, DB> Clone for AssistCtx<'a, DB> {
60:     fn clone(&self) -> Self {
61:         AssistCtx {
62:             db: self.db,
63:             frange: self.frange,
64:             source_file: self.source_file.clone(),
65:             should_compute_edit: self.should_compute_edit,
66:         }
67:     }
68: }
69: 
70: impl<'a, DB: HirDatabase> AssistCtx<'a, DB> {
71:     pub(crate) fn with_ctx<F, T>(db: &DB, frange: FileRange, should_compute_edit: bool, f: F) -> T
72:     where
73:         F: FnOnce(AssistCtx<DB>) -> T,
74:     {
75:         let parse = db.parse(frange.file_id);
76: 
77:         let ctx = AssistCtx { db, frange, source_file: parse.tree(), should_compute_edit };
78:         f(ctx)
79:     }

81:     pub(crate) fn add_assist(
82:         self,
83:         id: AssistId,
84:         label: impl Into<String>,
85:         f: impl FnOnce(&mut ActionBuilder),
86:     ) -> Option<Assist> {
87:         let label = AssistLabel { label: label.into(), id };
88:         assert!(label.label.chars().nth(0).unwrap().is_uppercase());
89: 
90:         let assist = if self.should_compute_edit {
91:             let action = {
92:                 let mut edit = ActionBuilder::default();
93:                 f(&mut edit);
94:                 edit.build()
95:             };
96:             Assist::Resolved { assist: ResolvedAssist { label, action_data: Either::Left(action) } }
97:         } else {
98:             Assist::Unresolved { label }
99:         };
100: 
101:         Some(assist)
102:     }
103:

105:     pub(crate) fn add_assist_group(
106:         self,
107:         id: AssistId,
108:         label: impl Into<String>,
109:         f: impl FnOnce() -> Vec<ActionBuilder>,
110:     ) -> Option<Assist> {
111:         let label = AssistLabel { label: label.into(), id };

116:             Assist::Resolved {
117:                 assist: ResolvedAssist {

119:                     action_data: Either::Right(

121:                     ),
122:                 },
123:             }
124:         } else {

1: //! This module handles fuzzy-searching of functions, structs and other symbols
2: //! by name across the whole workspace and dependencies.
3: //!
4: //! It works by building an incrementally-updated text-search index of all
5: //! symbols. The backbone of the index is the **awesome** `fst` crate by
6: //! @BurntSushi.
7: //!
8: //! In a nutshell, you give a set of strings to `fst`, and it builds a
9: //! finite state machine describing this set of strings. The strings which
10: //! could fuzzy-match a pattern can also be described by a finite state machine.
11: //! What is freaking cool is that you can now traverse both state machines in
12: //! lock-step to enumerate the strings which are both in the input set and
13: //! fuzz-match the query. Or, more formally, given two languages described by
14: //! FSTs, one can build a product FST which describes the intersection of the
15: //! languages.
16: //!
17: //! `fst` does not support cheap updating of the index, but it supports unioning
18: //! of state machines. So, to account for changing source code, we build an FST
19: //! for each library (which is assumed to never change) and an FST for each Rust
20: //! file in the current workspace, and run a query against the union of all
21: //! those FSTs.

23:     fmt,
24:     hash::{Hash, Hasher},
25:     mem,
26:     sync::Arc,

71: pub(crate) fn world_symbols(db: &RootDatabase, query: Query) -> Vec<FileSymbol> {
72:     /// Need to wrap Snapshot to provide `Clone` impl for `map_with`
73:     struct Snap(salsa::Snapshot<RootDatabase>);
74:     impl Clone for Snap {
75:         fn clone(&self) -> Snap {
76:             Snap(self.0.snapshot())
77:         }
78:     }

80:     let buf: Vec<Arc<SymbolIndex>> = if query.libs {
81:         let snap = Snap(db.snapshot());
82:         #[cfg(not(feature = "wasm"))]
83:         let buf = db
84:             .library_roots()
85:             .par_iter()
86:             .map_with(snap, |db, &lib_id| db.0.library_symbols(lib_id))
87:             .collect();
88: 
89:         #[cfg(feature = "wasm")]
90:         let buf = db.library_roots().iter().map(|&lib_id| snap.0.library_symbols(lib_id)).collect();
91: 
92:         buf
93:     } else {
94:         let mut files = Vec::new();
95:         for &root in db.local_roots().iter() {
96:             let sr = db.source_root(root);
97:             files.extend(sr.walk())
98:         }
99: 
100:         let snap = Snap(db.snapshot());
101:         #[cfg(not(feature = "wasm"))]
102:         let buf =
103:             files.par_iter().map_with(snap, |db, &file_id| db.0.file_symbols(file_id)).collect();
104: 
105:         #[cfg(feature = "wasm")]
106:         let buf = files.iter().map(|&file_id| snap.0.file_symbols(file_id)).collect();
107: 
108:         buf
109:     };
110:     query.search(&buf)

147: impl SymbolIndex {
148:     fn new(mut symbols: Vec<FileSymbol>) -> SymbolIndex {
149:         fn cmp_key<'a>(s1: &'a FileSymbol) -> impl Ord + 'a {
150:             unicase::Ascii::new(s1.name.as_str())
151:         }
152:         #[cfg(not(feature = "wasm"))]
153:         symbols.par_sort_by(|s1, s2| cmp_key(s1).cmp(&cmp_key(s2)));
154: 
155:         #[cfg(feature = "wasm")]
156:         symbols.sort_by(|s1, s2| cmp_key(s1).cmp(&cmp_key(s2)));
157: 
158:         let mut builder = fst::MapBuilder::memory();
159: 
160:         let mut last_batch_start = 0;
161: 
162:         for idx in 0..symbols.len() {
163:             if symbols.get(last_batch_start).map(cmp_key) == symbols.get(idx + 1).map(cmp_key) {
164:                 continue;
165:             }
166: 
167:             let start = last_batch_start;
168:             let end = idx + 1;
169:             last_batch_start = end;
170: 
171:             let key = symbols[start].name.as_str().to_lowercase();
172:             let value = SymbolIndex::range_to_map_value(start, end);
173: 
174:             builder.insert(key, value).unwrap();
175:         }
176: 
177:         let map = fst::Map::from_bytes(builder.into_inner().unwrap()).unwrap();
178:         SymbolIndex { symbols, map }
179:     }

209:     fn range_to_map_value(start: usize, end: usize) -> u64 {
210:         debug_assert![start <= (std::u32::MAX as usize)];
211:         debug_assert![end <= (std::u32::MAX as usize)];
212: 
213:         ((start as u64) << 32) | end as u64
214:     }

217:         let end = value as u32 as usize;
218:         let start = (value >> 32) as usize;
219:         (start, end)

223: impl Query {
224:     pub(crate) fn search(self, indices: &[Arc<SymbolIndex>]) -> Vec<FileSymbol> {
225:         let mut op = fst::map::OpBuilder::new();
226:         for file_symbols in indices.iter() {
227:             let automaton = fst::automaton::Subsequence::new(&self.lowercased);
228:             op = op.add(file_symbols.map.search(automaton))
229:         }
230:         let mut stream = op.union();
231:         let mut res = Vec::new();
232:         while let Some((_, indexed_values)) = stream.next() {
233:             if res.len() >= self.limit {
234:                 break;
235:             }
236:             for indexed_value in indexed_values {
237:                 let symbol_index = &indices[indexed_value.index];
238:                 let (start, end) = SymbolIndex::map_value_to_range(indexed_value.value);
239: 
240:                 for symbol in &symbol_index.symbols[start..end] {
241:                     if self.only_types && !is_type(symbol.ptr.kind()) {
242:                         continue;
243:                     }
244:                     if self.exact && symbol.name != self.query {
245:                         continue;
246:                     }
247:                     res.push(symbol.clone());
248:                 }
249:             }
250:         }
251:         res
252:     }
253: }

273: fn source_file_to_file_symbols(source_file: &SourceFile, file_id: FileId) -> Vec<FileSymbol> {
274:     let mut symbols = Vec::new();
275:     let mut stack = Vec::new();
276: 
277:     for event in source_file.syntax().preorder() {
278:         match event {
279:             WalkEvent::Enter(node) => {
280:                 if let Some(mut symbol) = to_file_symbol(&node, file_id) {
281:                     symbol.container_name = stack.last().cloned();
282: 
283:                     stack.push(symbol.name.clone());
284:                     symbols.push(symbol);
285:                 }
286:             }
287: 
288:             WalkEvent::Leave(node) => {
289:                 if to_symbol(&node).is_some() {
290:                     stack.pop();
291:                 }
292:             }
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     symbols
297: }

299: fn to_symbol(node: &SyntaxNode) -> Option<(SmolStr, SyntaxNodePtr, TextRange)> {
300:     fn decl<N: NameOwner>(node: N) -> Option<(SmolStr, SyntaxNodePtr, TextRange)> {
301:         let name = node.name()?;
302:         let name_range = name.syntax().text_range();
303:         let name = name.text().clone();
304:         let ptr = SyntaxNodePtr::new(node.syntax());
305: 
306:         Some((name, ptr, name_range))
307:     }
308:     match_ast! {
309:         match node {
310:             ast::FnDef(it) => { decl(it) },
311:             ast::StructDef(it) => { decl(it) },
312:             ast::EnumDef(it) => { decl(it) },
313:             ast::TraitDef(it) => { decl(it) },
314:             ast::Module(it) => { decl(it) },
315:             ast::TypeAliasDef(it) => { decl(it) },
316:             ast::ConstDef(it) => { decl(it) },
317:             ast::StaticDef(it) => { decl(it) },
318:             _ => None,
319:         }
320:     }
321: }
322: 
323: fn to_file_symbol(node: &SyntaxNode, file_id: FileId) -> Option<FileSymbol> {
324:     to_symbol(node).map(move |(name, ptr, name_range)| FileSymbol {
325:         name,
326:         ptr,
327:         file_id,
328:         name_range: Some(name_range),
329:         container_name: None,
330:     })

1: //! This module implements a reference search.
2: //! First, the element at the cursor position must be either an `ast::Name`
3: //! or `ast::NameRef`. If it's a `ast::NameRef`, at the classification step we
4: //! try to resolve the direct tree parent of this element, otherwise we
5: //! already have a definition and just need to get its HIR together with
6: //! some information that is needed for futher steps of searching.
7: //! After that, we collect files that might contain references and look
8: //! for text occurrences of the identifier. If there's an `ast::NameRef`
9: //! at the index that the match starts at and its tree parent is
10: //! resolved to the search element definition, we get a reference.

113: pub(crate) fn find_all_refs(
114:     db: &RootDatabase,
115:     mut position: FilePosition,
116:     search_scope: Option<SearchScope>,
117: ) -> Option<RangeInfo<ReferenceSearchResult>> {
118:     let parse = db.parse(position.file_id);
119:     let syntax = parse.tree().syntax().clone();
120: 
121:     let token = syntax.token_at_offset(position.offset);
122:     let mut search_kind = ReferenceKind::Other;
123: 
124:     if let TokenAtOffset::Between(ref left, ref right) = token {
125:         if (right.kind() == SyntaxKind::L_CURLY || right.kind() == SyntaxKind::L_PAREN)
126:             && left.kind() != SyntaxKind::IDENT
127:         {
128:             position = FilePosition { offset: left.text_range().start(), ..position };
129:             search_kind = ReferenceKind::StructLiteral;
130:         }
131:     }
132: 
133:     let RangeInfo { range, info: (name, def) } = find_name(db, &syntax, position)?;
134: 
135:     let declaration = match def.kind {
136:         NameKind::Macro(mac) => mac.to_nav(db),
137:         NameKind::Field(field) => field.to_nav(db),
138:         NameKind::AssocItem(assoc) => assoc.to_nav(db),
139:         NameKind::Def(def) => NavigationTarget::from_def(db, def)?,
140:         NameKind::SelfType(imp) => imp.to_nav(db),
141:         NameKind::Local(local) => local.to_nav(db),
142:         NameKind::TypeParam(_) => return None,
143:     };
144: 
145:     let search_scope = {
146:         let base = def.search_scope(db);
147:         match search_scope {
148:             None => base,
149:             Some(scope) => base.intersection(&scope),
150:         }
151:     };
152: 
153:     let decl_range = declaration.range();
154: 
155:     let declaration = Declaration {
156:         nav: declaration,
157:         kind: ReferenceKind::Other,
158:         access: decl_access(&def.kind, &name, &syntax, decl_range),
159:     };
160: 
161:     let references = process_definition(db, def, name, search_scope)
162:         .into_iter()
163:         .filter(|r| search_kind == ReferenceKind::Other || search_kind == r.kind)
164:         .collect();
165: 
166:     Some(RangeInfo::new(range, ReferenceSearchResult { declaration, references }))
167: }

169: fn find_name(
170:     db: &RootDatabase,
171:     syntax: &SyntaxNode,
172:     position: FilePosition,
173: ) -> Option<RangeInfo<(String, NameDefinition)>> {
174:     let mut sb = SourceBinder::new(db);
175:     if let Some(name) = find_node_at_offset::<ast::Name>(&syntax, position.offset) {
176:         let def = classify_name(&mut sb, InFile::new(position.file_id.into(), &name))?;
177:         let range = name.syntax().text_range();
178:         return Some(RangeInfo::new(range, (name.text().to_string(), def)));
179:     }
180:     let name_ref = find_node_at_offset::<ast::NameRef>(&syntax, position.offset)?;
181:     let def = classify_name_ref(&mut sb, InFile::new(position.file_id.into(), &name_ref))?;
182:     let range = name_ref.syntax().text_range();
183:     Some(RangeInfo::new(range, (name_ref.text().to_string(), def)))
184: }

186: fn process_definition(
187:     db: &RootDatabase,
188:     def: NameDefinition,
189:     name: String,
190:     scope: SearchScope,
191: ) -> Vec<Reference> {
192:     let _p = profile("process_definition");
193: 
194:     let pat = name.as_str();
195:     let mut refs = vec![];
196: 
197:     for (file_id, search_range) in scope {
198:         let text = db.file_text(file_id);
199: 
200:         let parse = Lazy::new(|| SourceFile::parse(&text));
201:         let mut sb = Lazy::new(|| SourceBinder::new(db));
202: 
203:         for (idx, _) in text.match_indices(pat) {
204:             let offset = TextUnit::from_usize(idx);
205: 
206:             if let Some(name_ref) =
207:                 find_node_at_offset::<ast::NameRef>(parse.tree().syntax(), offset)
208:             {
209:                 let range = name_ref.syntax().text_range();
210:                 if let Some(search_range) = search_range {
211:                     if !range.is_subrange(&search_range) {
212:                         continue;
213:                     }
214:                 }
215:                 // FIXME: reuse sb
216:                 // See https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/68198#issuecomment-574269098
217: 
218:                 if let Some(d) = classify_name_ref(&mut sb, InFile::new(file_id.into(), &name_ref))
219:                 {
220:                     if d == def {
221:                         let kind = if name_ref
222:                             .syntax()
223:                             .ancestors()
224:                             .find_map(ast::RecordLit::cast)
225:                             .and_then(|l| l.path())
226:                             .and_then(|p| p.segment())
227:                             .and_then(|p| p.name_ref())
228:                             .map(|n| n == name_ref)
229:                             .unwrap_or(false)
230:                         {
231:                             ReferenceKind::StructLiteral
232:                         } else {
233:                             ReferenceKind::Other
234:                         };
235: 
236:                         refs.push(Reference {
237:                             file_range: FileRange { file_id, range },
238:                             kind,
239:                             access: reference_access(&d.kind, &name_ref),
240:                         });
241:                     }
242:                 }
243:             }
244:         }
245:     }
246:     refs
247: }

249: fn decl_access(
250:     kind: &NameKind,
251:     name: &str,
252:     syntax: &SyntaxNode,
253:     range: TextRange,
254: ) -> Option<ReferenceAccess> {
255:     match kind {
256:         NameKind::Local(_) | NameKind::Field(_) => {}
257:         _ => return None,
258:     };
259: 
260:     let stmt = find_node_at_offset::<ast::LetStmt>(syntax, range.start())?;
261:     if let Some(_) = stmt.initializer() {
262:         let pat = stmt.pat()?;
263:         if let ast::Pat::BindPat(it) = pat {
264:             if it.name()?.text().as_str() == name {
265:                 return Some(ReferenceAccess::Write);
266:             }
267:         }
268:     }
269: 
270:     None
271: }

273: fn reference_access(kind: &NameKind, name_ref: &ast::NameRef) -> Option<ReferenceAccess> {
274:     // Only Locals and Fields have accesses for now.
275:     match kind {
276:         NameKind::Local(_) | NameKind::Field(_) => {}
277:         _ => return None,
278:     };
279: 
280:     let mode = name_ref.syntax().ancestors().find_map(|node| {
281:         match_ast! {
282:             match (node) {
283:                 ast::BinExpr(expr) => {
284:                     if expr.op_kind()?.is_assignment() {
285:                         // If the variable or field ends on the LHS's end then it's a Write (covers fields and locals).
286:                         // FIXME: This is not terribly accurate.
287:                         if let Some(lhs) = expr.lhs() {
288:                             if lhs.syntax().text_range().end() == name_ref.syntax().text_range().end() {
289:                                 return Some(ReferenceAccess::Write);
290:                             }
291:                         }
292:                     }
293:                     Some(ReferenceAccess::Read)
294:                 },
295:                 _ => {None}
296:             }
297:         }
298:     });
299: 
300:     // Default Locals and Fields to read
301:     mode.or(Some(ReferenceAccess::Read))
302: }

80: fn collect_path_segments_raw(
81:     segments: &mut Vec<ast::PathSegment>,
82:     mut path: ast::Path,
83: ) -> Option<usize> {
84:     let oldlen = segments.len();
85:     loop {
86:         let mut children = path.syntax().children_with_tokens();
87:         let (first, second, third) = (
88:             children.next().map(|n| (n.clone(), n.kind())),
89:             children.next().map(|n| (n.clone(), n.kind())),
90:             children.next().map(|n| (n.clone(), n.kind())),
91:         );
92:         match (first, second, third) {
93:             (Some((subpath, PATH)), Some((_, T![::])), Some((segment, PATH_SEGMENT))) => {
94:                 path = ast::Path::cast(subpath.as_node()?.clone())?;
95:                 segments.push(ast::PathSegment::cast(segment.as_node()?.clone())?);
96:             }
97:             (Some((segment, PATH_SEGMENT)), _, _) => {
98:                 segments.push(ast::PathSegment::cast(segment.as_node()?.clone())?);
99:                 break;
100:             }
101:             (_, _, _) => return None,
102:         }
103:     }
104:     // We need to reverse only the new added segments
105:     let only_new_segments = segments.split_at_mut(oldlen).1;
106:     only_new_segments.reverse();
107:     Some(segments.len() - oldlen)
108: }

269:     };
270: 
271:     // This can happen only if current_use_tree is a direct child of a UseItem
272:     if let Some(name) = alias.and_then(|it| it.name()) {
273:         if compare_path_segment_with_name(&target[0], &name) {
274:             return ImportAction::Nothing;
275:         }
276:     }
277: 
278:     collect_path_segments_raw(current_path_segments, path.clone());
279: 
280:     // We compare only the new segments added in the line just above.
281:     // The first prev_len segments were already compared in 'parent' recursive calls.
282:     let left = target.split_at(prev_len).1;
283:     let right = current_path_segments.split_at(prev_len).1;
284:     let common = compare_path_segments(left, &right);
285:     let mut action = match common {
286:         0 => ImportAction::add_new_use(
287:             // e.g: target is std::fmt and we can have
288:             // use foo::bar
289:             // We add a brand new use statement
290:             current_use_tree
291:                 .syntax()
292:                 .ancestors()
293:                 .find_map(ast::UseItem::cast)
294:                 .map(|it| it.syntax().clone()),
295:             true,
296:         ),
297:         common if common == left.len() && left.len() == right.len() => {
298:             // e.g: target is std::fmt and we can have
299:             // 1- use std::fmt;
300:             // 2- use std::fmt::{ ... }
301:             if let Some(list) = tree_list {
302:                 // In case 2 we need to add self to the nested list
303:                 // unless it's already there
304:                 let has_self = list.use_trees().map(|it| it.path()).any(|p| {
305:                     p.and_then(|it| it.segment())
306:                         .and_then(|it| it.kind())
307:                         .filter(|k| *k == ast::PathSegmentKind::SelfKw)
308:                         .is_some()
309:                 });
310: 
311:                 if has_self {
312:                     ImportAction::Nothing
313:                 } else {
314:                     ImportAction::add_in_tree_list(current_path_segments.len(), list, true)
315:                 }
316:             } else {
317:                 // Case 1
318:                 ImportAction::Nothing
319:             }
320:         }
321:         common if common != left.len() && left.len() == right.len() => {
322:             // e.g: target is std::fmt and we have
323:             // use std::io;
324:             // We need to split.
325:             let segments_to_split = current_path_segments.split_at(prev_len + common).1;
326:             ImportAction::add_nested_import(
327:                 prev_len + common,
328:                 path,
329:                 Some(segments_to_split[0].clone()),
330:                 false,
331:             )
332:         }
333:         common if common == right.len() && left.len() > right.len() => {
334:             // e.g: target is std::fmt and we can have
335:             // 1- use std;
336:             // 2- use std::{ ... };
337: 
338:             // fallback action
339:             let mut better_action = ImportAction::add_new_use(
340:                 current_use_tree
341:                     .syntax()
342:                     .ancestors()
343:                     .find_map(ast::UseItem::cast)
344:                     .map(|it| it.syntax().clone()),
345:                 true,
346:             );
347:             if let Some(list) = tree_list {
348:                 // Case 2, check recursively if the path is already imported in the nested list
349:                 for u in list.use_trees() {
350:                     let child_action = walk_use_tree_for_best_action(
351:                         current_path_segments,
352:                         Some(list.clone()),
353:                         u,
354:                         target,
355:                     );
356:                     if child_action.is_better(&better_action) {
357:                         better_action = child_action;
358:                         if let ImportAction::Nothing = better_action {
359:                             return better_action;
360:                         }
361:                     }
362:                 }
363:             } else {
364:                 // Case 1, split adding self
365:                 better_action = ImportAction::add_nested_import(prev_len + common, path, None, true)
366:             }
367:             better_action
368:         }
369:         common if common == left.len() && left.len() < right.len() => {
370:             // e.g: target is std::fmt and we can have
371:             // use std::fmt::Debug;
372:             let segments_to_split = current_path_segments.split_at(prev_len + common).1;
373:             ImportAction::add_nested_import(
374:                 prev_len + common,
375:                 path,
376:                 Some(segments_to_split[0].clone()),
377:                 true,
378:             )
379:         }
380:         common if common < left.len() && common < right.len() => {
381:             // e.g: target is std::fmt::nested::Debug
382:             // use std::fmt::Display
383:             let segments_to_split = current_path_segments.split_at(prev_len + common).1;
384:             ImportAction::add_nested_import(
385:                 prev_len + common,
386:                 path,
387:                 Some(segments_to_split[0].clone()),
388:                 false,
389:             )
390:         }
391:         _ => unreachable!(),
392:     };
393: 
394:     // If we are inside a UseTreeList adding a use statement become adding to the existing
395:     // tree list.
396:     action = match (current_parent_use_tree_list, action.clone()) {
397:         (Some(use_tree_list), ImportAction::AddNewUse { .. }) => {
398:             ImportAction::add_in_tree_list(prev_len, use_tree_list, false)
399:         }
400:         (_, _) => action,
401:     };
402: 
403:     // We remove the segments added
404:     current_path_segments.truncate(prev_len);
405:     action
406: }

408: fn best_action_for_target(
409:     container: SyntaxNode,
410:     anchor: SyntaxNode,
411:     target: &[SmolStr],
412: ) -> ImportAction {
413:     let mut storage = Vec::with_capacity(16); // this should be the only allocation
414:     let best_action = container
415:         .children()
416:         .filter_map(ast::UseItem::cast)
417:         .filter_map(|it| it.use_tree())
418:         .map(|u| walk_use_tree_for_best_action(&mut storage, None, u, target))
419:         .fold(None, |best, a| match best {
420:             Some(best) => Some(ImportAction::better(best, a)),
421:             None => Some(a),
422:         });
423: 
424:     match best_action {
425:         Some(action) => action,
426:         None => {
427:             // We have no action and no UseItem was found in container so we find
428:             // another item and we use it as anchor.
429:             // If there are no items above, we choose the target path itself as anchor.
430:             // todo: we should include even whitespace blocks as anchor candidates
431:             let anchor = container
432:                 .children()
433:                 .find(|n| n.text_range().start() < anchor.text_range().start())
434:                 .or_else(|| Some(anchor));
435: 
436:             ImportAction::add_new_use(anchor, false)
437:         }
438:     }
439: }

441: fn make_assist(action: &ImportAction, target: &[SmolStr], edit: &mut TextEditBuilder) {
442:     match action {
443:         ImportAction::AddNewUse { anchor, add_after_anchor } => {
444:             make_assist_add_new_use(anchor, *add_after_anchor, target, edit)
445:         }
446:         ImportAction::AddInTreeList { common_segments, tree_list, add_self } => {
447:             // We know that the fist n segments already exists in the use statement we want
448:             // to modify, so we want to add only the last target.len() - n segments.
449:             let segments_to_add = target.split_at(*common_segments).1;
450:             make_assist_add_in_tree_list(tree_list, segments_to_add, *add_self, edit)
451:         }
452:         ImportAction::AddNestedImport {
453:             common_segments,
454:             path_to_split,
455:             first_segment_to_split,
456:             add_self,
457:         } => {
458:             let segments_to_add = target.split_at(*common_segments).1;
459:             make_assist_add_nested_import(
460:                 path_to_split,
461:                 first_segment_to_split,
462:                 segments_to_add,
463:                 *add_self,
464:                 edit,
465:             )
466:         }
467:         _ => {}
468:     }
469: }

471: fn make_assist_add_new_use(
472:     anchor: &Option<SyntaxNode>,
473:     after: bool,
474:     target: &[SmolStr],
475:     edit: &mut TextEditBuilder,
476: ) {
477:     if let Some(anchor) = anchor {
478:         let indent = ra_fmt::leading_indent(anchor);
479:         let mut buf = String::new();
480:         if after {
481:             buf.push_str("\n");
482:             if let Some(spaces) = &indent {
483:                 buf.push_str(spaces);
484:             }
485:         }
486:         buf.push_str("use ");
487:         fmt_segments_raw(target, &mut buf);
488:         buf.push_str(";");
489:         if !after {
490:             buf.push_str("\n\n");
491:             if let Some(spaces) = &indent {
492:                 buf.push_str(&spaces);
493:             }
494:         }
495:         let position = if after { anchor.text_range().end() } else { anchor.text_range().start() };
496:         edit.insert(position, buf);
497:     }
498: }

500: fn make_assist_add_in_tree_list(
501:     tree_list: &ast::UseTreeList,
502:     target: &[SmolStr],
503:     add_self: bool,
504:     edit: &mut TextEditBuilder,
505: ) {
506:     let last = tree_list.use_trees().last();
507:     if let Some(last) = last {
508:         let mut buf = String::new();
509:         let comma = last.syntax().siblings(Direction::Next).find(|n| n.kind() == T![,]);
510:         let offset = if let Some(comma) = comma {
511:             comma.text_range().end()
512:         } else {
513:             buf.push_str(",");
514:             last.syntax().text_range().end()
515:         };
516:         if add_self {
517:             buf.push_str(" self")
518:         } else {
519:             buf.push_str(" ");
520:         }
521:         fmt_segments_raw(target, &mut buf);
522:         edit.insert(offset, buf);
523:     } else {
524:     }
525: }

527: fn make_assist_add_nested_import(
528:     path: &ast::Path,
529:     first_segment_to_split: &Option<ast::PathSegment>,
530:     target: &[SmolStr],
531:     add_self: bool,
532:     edit: &mut TextEditBuilder,
533: ) {
534:     let use_tree = path.syntax().ancestors().find_map(ast::UseTree::cast);
535:     if let Some(use_tree) = use_tree {
536:         let (start, add_colon_colon) = if let Some(first_segment_to_split) = first_segment_to_split
537:         {
538:             (first_segment_to_split.syntax().text_range().start(), false)
539:         } else {
540:             (use_tree.syntax().text_range().end(), true)
541:         };
542:         let end = use_tree.syntax().text_range().end();
543: 
544:         let mut buf = String::new();
545:         if add_colon_colon {
546:             buf.push_str("::");
547:         }
548:         buf.push_str("{");
549:         if add_self {
550:             buf.push_str("self, ");
551:         }
552:         fmt_segments_raw(target, &mut buf);
553:         if !target.is_empty() {
554:             buf.push_str(", ");
555:         }
556:         edit.insert(start, buf);
557:         edit.insert(end, "}".to_string());
558:     }
559: }

561: fn apply_auto_import(
562:     container: &SyntaxNode,
563:     path: &ast::Path,
564:     target: &[SmolStr],
565:     edit: &mut TextEditBuilder,
566: ) {
567:     let action = best_action_for_target(container.clone(), path.syntax().clone(), target);
568:     make_assist(&action, target, edit);
569:     if let Some(last) = path.segment() {
570:         // Here we are assuming the assist will provide a  correct use statement
571:         // so we can delete the path qualifier
572:         edit.delete(TextRange::from_to(
573:             path.syntax().text_range().start(),
574:             last.syntax().text_range().start(),
575:         ));
576:     }
577: }

579: fn collect_hir_path_segments(path: &hir::Path) -> Option<Vec<SmolStr>> {
580:     let mut ps = Vec::<SmolStr>::with_capacity(10);
581:     match path.kind() {
582:         hir::PathKind::Abs => ps.push("".into()),
583:         hir::PathKind::Crate => ps.push("crate".into()),
584:         hir::PathKind::Plain => {}
585:         hir::PathKind::Super(0) => ps.push("self".into()),
586:         hir::PathKind::Super(lvl) => {
587:             let mut chain = "super".to_string();
588:             for _ in 0..*lvl {
589:                 chain += "::super";
590:             }
591:             ps.push(chain.into());
592:         }
593:         hir::PathKind::DollarCrate(_) => return None,
594:     }
595:     ps.extend(path.segments().iter().map(|it| it.name.to_string().into()));
596:     Some(ps)
597: }

167:         PathResolution::Def(def) => Some(from_module_def(sb.db, def, Some(container))),
